reading.body:
America's Credit Unions filed 8 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports naming AI, and 23 lobbyists appear across them, 10 on all 8 filings.

The pattern is concentration. A single client, the Credit Union National Association, produced 8 AI filings through one registered firm, and the same ten lobbyists are named on every one. The remaining thirteen appear on between one and five filings each, which reads as a core team carrying the account with others rotating in. Two bills are named, HR 2152 and HR 4801, both from 2025 or later.

For AI specifically, this shows a financial trade association treating AI as a standing lobbying subject rather than a one-off. Credit unions sit on the compliance side of AI in lending, fraud detection, and member data, so their interest is in how AI rules reach small institutions. That is a governance and paperwork concern, not a compute or power one. Nothing here ties this client to data centers, electricity, or chip supply.

What the data does not say is what position the association argued. A filing reports that a firm lobbied on an issue, not the stance taken, so the 8 filings establish attention and its intensity, not direction. The data also covers only this one client and firm, with no dollar amounts, no agency targets, and no text of the bills.
